domestic.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story / style-transfer. Production raster sprite atlas for the EXISTING Trætoppen game interiors. Image 1 (buildings.png) is the authoritative hand-painted building and material style; Image 2 (heroes.png) is the authoritative character scale and soft contour reference; Image 3 (interior_terrain.png) is the exact floor palette. Derive new interior furnishing artwork from these references. Match detailed matte storybook gouache/watercolor, gently uneven warm grey-brown pencil contours, worn honey oak, cream plaster, sage and muted lavender textiles, restrained terracotta, little handmade details and subtle paper tooth. Inspiration from Stardew Valley is ONLY cozy lived-in furnishings, clear silhouettes, legible functional objects and a comforting sense of home; retain our illustrated style and our elevated isometric camera, no pixel art and no copied game objects. Fixed orthographic camera at 36 degrees elevation, looking at the front and right; ground circles are ellipses about .59 as tall as wide. Single objects, complete silhouettes, generous transparent gutters, no walls, room scene, floor bases, cast shadows, people, letters, captions, logos or visible grid. True transparent background. Neutral albedo, engine supplies day/night lighting. Every listed object must form one substantial connected alpha island. No glossy 3D render, plastic, black vector outlines or photorealism.
Create ONE 2048x1536 atlas in a STRICT 4 COLUMN by 3 ROW grid of TWELVE distinct extractable objects, row-major:
1. Very simple low pine single bed with irregular patched sage quilt, cream pillow, tiny humble wood headboard; entire bed including feet.
2. Better honey-oak double bed, a neat muted lavender and cream patchwork quilt, two cream pillows, rounded carved headboard; entire bed.
3. Small round honey-oak dining table on four stout legs, tiny cream teapot and two cups placed on it, no chairs.
4. One small rustic wooden dining chair, pale sage seat cushion, three simple back slats, complete legs.
5. A cozy two-seat curved sage fabric sofa, honey wood feet, two cream cushions and folded lavender throw, no rug.
6. A squat cottage stone hearth with small brass stove door, inset warm orange embers, a little stack of logs tucked into its side, no wall or mantle decorations outside the silhouette.
7. A tall freestanding cottage kitchen hutch, cream painted wood with honey timber top, shelves of ceramic plates, two hanging copper pans attached to its own backboard, doors below; no room wall.
8. A medium rustic honey wood bookshelf, uneven books and a little fern in a pot on its top, no wall.
9. A rounded double-door wood wardrobe with tiny brass handles and simple leaf carving, muted warm wood, complete base.
10. A small broad oak storage chest with arched lid, iron straps, tiny keyhole and worn edges; closed.
11. A clay pot with a lush soft sage trailing houseplant, complete foliage and pot, no hanging rope.
12. A compact rustic hand loom on its own short timber legs, partly woven cream and muted sage cloth, little attached spool. No chair.
Keep objects broad and readable beside our fox character. Beds are usable beds with open foot ends, not decorative dollhouse miniatures.

walls.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story / style-transfer. Production modular interior WALL SURFACE masters for the existing Trætoppen game. Image 1 buildings.png and Image 2 interior_domestic.png are exact painted style references; Image 3 interior_terrain.png supplies matching floor pigments. Detailed matte gouache/watercolor, warm grey-brown thin pencil seams, softly worn wood, subtle paper tooth, cream, sage, warm honey, muted lavender. Stardew Valley inspires the cozy live-in material choices only; no pixel art, copied assets or 3D render.
Create ONE 2048x1536 transparent atlas, strict 4 COLUMN by 2 ROW grid of EIGHT separate flat FRONT-FACING RECTANGULAR wall panel paintings. These are flat material panels for later deterministic projection onto our existing isometric wall geometry. NO perspective, isometric side faces, room scenes, floor, cast shadows or freestanding objects. Each panel is a tall rectangle about .65 as wide as high with its entire rectangular silhouette contained in its own invisible grid cell with a transparent gutter. Inside each rectangle paint all the way to its four edges, opaque. All panels share the same panel height proportions: simple thin ceiling moulding at top, an upper wall, a chair rail at 35 percent above bottom and matching low wainscot with skirting. Match surface pattern at the left and right edge so repeated panels can join.
Top row, four plain wall panels left to right:
1. Humble warm honey vertical pine boards, worn grain and a few quiet knots, dark timber skirting and top trim.
2. Cozy cream lime plaster, delicate tiny sage sprig wallpaper marks, warm oak lower wainscot and honey chair rail; cottage / farm-house material.
3. Elegant warm ivory paper with faint muted sage and lavender leaf damask, cream lower panels, thin warm brass accent, restrained manor quality.
4. Warm ivory marble blocks with subtle pale lavender veins, ivory lower panels with tiny brass trim, intimate storybook palace quality, not shiny.
Bottom row repeats the SAME four material panels in the SAME order, but each has one complete small inset window centred in its UPPER area. Window glass is quiet cool blue/teal with just a soft pale reflection, not bright amber. Humble plank has a plain rounded wood frame, cottage plaster has a small arched oak frame and attached short cream curtains, manor has a slightly taller arched cream wood frame with tiny brass latch, marble has a slender original pointed leaf-arch frame with quiet brass trim. Keep all window frames/curtains within the panel and keep the mouldings, chair rail and skirting heights identical to the matching plain panel above.
No words, labels, numbers, characters, halos, ray beams or perspective. All eight rectangles isolated on true transparency.
